reproduction_target: Computational analysis of a newly developed massively parallel reporter assay (QUASARR-seq, plus its SOLARR-seq variant) that measures intrinsic promoter and enhancer activity of the same transcriptional regulatory elements (TREs) simultaneously in K-562. Computational target: TRE definition/selection from PRO-cap TSSs, DNase-seq DHSs and GENCODE proximity; read filtering with fastp (exact flags given); eaBC-TRE-paBC index mapping and RNA/DNA barcode activity measurement with 'biodatatools' (commands stated to live in an Extended Text supplement); edgeR normalization to logFCs; a custom 'uniform active element call pipeline' (CPM prefilter, ORF-only modified TMM, limma-voom log2(RNA/DNA), Z-score vs negative controls in both orientations); activity boost index, activity balance index, GC content, PWM motif match score and delta-boost index formulas; PRO-cap/PRO-seq UMI-deduplicated signal quantification; benchmarking against SuRE / lentiMPRA / ATAC-STARR-seq / WHG-STARR-seq by reciprocal overlap; RT-qPCR delta-Cq read-through estimation; re-analysis of a published CRISPRa HS2/HBG1 dataset; and the reported statistics (Spearman, Student's and one-sample t-tests, Cohen's d, ANOVA, Bland-Altman). Vector engineering, TRE cloning, barcode-library construction, cell culture/nucleofection, harvest-time optimization, library preparation + NovaSeq X Plus sequencing and the RT-qPCR bench work are wet-lab (W, out of scope for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis list built from the bioRxiv v2 JATS XML full text (fetched with curl + browser user-agent into an isolated per-paper scratch directory; 156 KB; title phrase 'regulatory reciprocity' and 'functional duality' confirmed present, so the fetch is the correct paper). The paper HAS both a Data availability and a Code availability statement, but both are forward-looking promises: 'QUASARR-seq data will be made available in the ENCODE portal', 'PRO-seq data will be made available in the ENCODE portal', 'All accession codes not provided will be made available prior to publication', and 'Code will be made available on GitHub prior to publication'. No repository URL, no DOI and no accession for any newly generated dataset appears anywhere in the manuscript. Four ENCODE accessions are given, all for datasets RETRIEVED (not generated): ENCSR220XSM (PRO-cap), ENCSR382BVV (lentiMPRA), ENCSR312UQM (ATAC-STARR-seq), ENCSR661FOW (WHG-STARR-seq). Only four software names appear in the whole text (fastp, biodatatools, edgeR, limma-voom) and NONE carries a version number; no genome build (hg38/GRCh38), no GENCODE release and no R/Python version is stated anywhere. Code axis is scored 1 ('reconstructable') where the prose or an explicitly stated formula gives an operational description, never 2, because no code is deposited. Wet-lab steps counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: TRE definition and selection: candidate active/inactive promoters vs enhancers defined from PRO-cap TSSs, DNase-seq DHSs and distance to GENCODE annotation in K-562 (<500 bp proximal, >500 bp distal; transcribed elements cloned 60 bp downstream of each divergent TSS peak maximum) - no genome build, no GENCODE release, no DNase-seq accession, no peak-calling tool named
Raw QUASARR-seq/SOLARR-seq read filtering with fastp using the verbatim parameters '--disable_adapter_trimming --trim_poly_g --cut_right' - exact flags given, no fastp version

eaBC-TRE-paBC index mapping with 'biodatatools': barcode/UMI extraction per library layout, eaBC/paBC clustering by merging sequences within Hamming distance 1, alignment of partial element sequences to reference element sequences, barcode-to-TRE assignment (plus a 3-bp minP barcode for the multi-minP library set) - 'detailed commands and workflow found in the Extended Text', not in a repository; no biodatatools version

RNA aBC / DNA aBC activity measurement with 'biodatatools': barcode extraction, matching to the clustered index, TRE assignment and UMI collapse of identical copies - commands again deferred to the Extended Text; no version, no UMI-collapse parameters stated in the main text

Normalization of RNA and DNA element counts with edgeR to obtain normalized element counts and logFCs - single-sentence mention; no edgeR version, no normalization method, no design/dispersion settings, no filtering thresholds
Activity boost index calculation from promoter/enhancer logFCs relative to the mean activity of negative-control ORFs - formula given in Methods; no software, no script

Uniform active element call pipeline ('as previously described', ref 27): CPM prefilter at a threshold derived from a raw count of 10 in the smallest DNA library, ORF-only modified TMM normalization, log2(RNA aBCs/DNA aBCs) via limma-voom, then a Z-score comparison against negative controls in both orientations to call active enhancers and promoters - the significance criterion ('significantly higher') is never defined (no Z or p cutoff, no multiple-testing correction); pipeline code is not deposited

Activity balance index: Z-score normalization of promoter and enhancer boost indices followed by classification (promoter-dominant Bal > 1, enhancer-dominant Bal < -1, balanced -1 <= Bal <= 1) - formula and thresholds given; no software, no script

GC content calculation over tested element sequences - formula given; element sequence set itself is not deposited (Supplementary Table 1 lists primers, not element coordinates/sequences); no software

Motif match score as a PWM-vs-background log-odds ratio; PWMs taken from Adato & Sloutskin et al. (ElemeNT 2023) and background base frequencies computed across K-562 GRO-cap peaks from Core & Martins et al. - no ElemeNT/PWM database version, no accession for the GRO-cap peak set, no pseudocount, no scan window or score cutoff, no software

Change (delta) boost index calculation: mutant boost index minus wild-type boost index, for disease-associated (n=9), synthetic (n=3), GWAS (n=4) and population (n=8) variants - formula given; variant coordinates given only for the APC c.-192A>G example (ClinVar ID 243006) and the three synthetic YY1-motif mutants; no table of the remaining variants; no software

PRO-cap / PRO-seq signal quantification: UMI-deduplicated read counts inside tested-element boundaries (PRO-cap) and twelve enumerated PRO-seq window variants (total/mean counts at 100/250/500 bp downstream-for-forward, upstream-for-reverse, with and without boundary extension) - window definitions fully enumerated, but no counting tool, no deduplication tool, no genome build, and the PRO-seq data itself is undeposited

Benchmarking against orthogonal assays: elements compared at >=10% reciprocal overlap with SuRE and >=50% reciprocal overlap with lentiMPRA (ENCSR382BVV), ATAC-STARR-seq (ENCSR312UQM) and WHG-STARR-seq (ENCSR661FOW), with active enhancer calls re-derived through the same uniform active call pipeline - overlap thresholds given, but no overlap tool (bedtools or similar), no genome build, and processed SuRE data cited only to van Arensbergen et al. with no accession

RT-qPCR data processing and read-through transcription estimation: technical-replicate Cq averaging, delta-Cq relative expression of luc2 vs egfp, RQ with SD/SEM across replicates, and the read-through fraction from RQ_Empty vs RQ_TRE (reported as 16.47% of egfp expression) - formulas given, but the underlying Cq/RQ source tables are not deposited anywhere and no analysis software is named

Reported statistical analyses: Spearman correlations, Student's t-test, one-sample t-test with Cohen's d, ANOVA (F(2,8296) etc.), replicate R-squared, and Bland-Altman agreement analysis - tests are named with test statistics but no statistical software, no version, no seed and no code; there is no dedicated statistics Methods subsection

Re-analysis of a published CRISPRa dataset (Wang et al., ref 32): correlation of HS2 eRNA activation against HBG1 mRNA activation across dCas9-VPR/SAM/SunTag/p300/CBP and dCas9 control (Spearman rho = 0.79) - the processed CRISPRa RT- and ChIP-qPCR data were 'obtained from I. Hilton, Rice University' by personal communication, with no repository, accession or supplementary deposit; no analysis code
QUASARR-seq vector design and engineering (pDEST-QUASARR-luc-gfp-pMYC and the pGAPDH / pAPOBEC3F / pADGRG5 minP variants, pDEST-luc-pMYC-preBC and -CCW surrogates)
TRE cloning: batch primer design with an unnamed in-house web tool, PCR from K-562 genomic DNA, Gateway BP/LR cloning, sequence verification and en masse library propagation
eaBC-TRE-paBC high-complexity index generation: consecutive isothermal oligo extensions, HiFi assembly, transformation and colony-scale complexity control (>=10 barcodes per TRE)
K-562 cell culture and nucleofection (Amaxa Nucleofector II, program T-016; 5 electroporations per technical replicate, 3 technical replicates per biological replicate; 6 h incubation)
Optimal harvest time time-course experiments (2-48 hpt) establishing 6 hpt as the standard harvest point

QUASARR-seq library preparation (TRIzol RNA extraction, DNase I, SuperScript III RT, Hirt plasmid DNA extraction, two primer extensions with Exonuclease I cleanup, low-cycle adapter PCR) and 2 x 150 bp sequencing on an Illumina NovaSeq X Plus
SOLARR-seq construct generation and assay (QUASARR-seq vector without the paBC/egfp promoter-readout module, early pAs downstream of the TRE cassette)
RT-qPCR bench work targeting luc2 and egfp (LunaScript RT, Luna qPCR master mix, QuantStudio 7 Pro, no-RT controls)

headline.static_readiness: 0/16 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 3/16 computational steps (C2 fastp with verbatim flags, C3 and C4 biodatatools index mapping / activity measurement whose commands are deferred to an Extended Text supplement) - these reach RI only because a software package is at least NAMED and at least one operational parameter is stated; not one of them carries a version number. 13/16 steps cap at NI. The dominant blocker is uniform: there is no analysis code anywhere ('Code will be made available on GitHub prior to publication'), the primary QUASARR-seq/SOLARR-seq/PRO-seq data are not yet deposited ('will be made available in the ENCODE portal', no accession), only four software names appear in the entire manuscript and none is versioned, and no genome build or GENCODE release is ever stated. Nine steps are pure formulas (boost index, balance index, GC content, motif match score, delta-boost index, RT-qPCR delta-Cq) that are fully written out in Methods but attributed to no software at all, which is why they sit at version=0 rather than at RI. No lockfile, container digest or conda specification is claimed, so no step could exceed RI even under Stage 2; capture_claim is 'floating' and stage2_candidate is false.
headline.coverage: 16 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v2 JATS XML Methods prose (element selection, read filtering, barcode index mapping, activity measurement, normalization, active-element calling, five index/score formulas, PRO-cap/PRO-seq quantification, orthogonal-assay benchmarking, RT-qPCR processing, statistics, published-CRISPRa re-analysis). 8 wet-lab step groups counted in W but out of computational-reproduction scope: vector engineering, TRE cloning, barcode-library construction, cell culture/nucleofection, harvest-time optimization, QUASARR-seq library prep + NovaSeq X Plus sequencing, SOLARR-seq assay construction, and RT-qPCR bench work. Computational coverage = 16/24 = 67%.

gaps.where: Whole analysis pipeline (Code availability section, verbatim: 'Code will be made available on GitHub prior to publication.')
gaps.missing: No code is deposited or linked. No repository URL, organization, DOI or archive appears anywhere in the manuscript - a full-text search for 'github', 'gitlab', 'zenodo', 'bitbucket' returns only this single forward-looking sentence. This covers the QUASARR-seq preprocessing pipeline (developed by A.K-Y.L.), the uniform activity calling pipeline (developed by J.Z.), and all downstream index/score calculations and figure code.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the preprocessing pipeline, the uniform active element call pipeline and the downstream analysis/figure scripts in a public repository with a tagged release or Zenodo DOI, and replace the promise with a resolvable URL in the Code availability statement.

gaps.where: Data availability - all newly generated data (QUASARR-seq, SOLARR-seq, PRO-seq, and the RT-qPCR Cq tables)
gaps.missing: Verbatim: 'QUASARR-seq data will be made available in the ENCODE portal', 'PRO-seq data will be made available in the ENCODE portal', 'All accession codes not provided will be made available prior to publication.' No accession, no DOI and no embargo release date is given for any dataset generated in this study, so the primary input to every computational step is currently unobtainable. The RT-qPCR Cq/RQ source tables (C14) are not mentioned in the availability statement at all. The tested-element coordinate/sequence table and the variant list behind C11 are likewise not deposited (Supplementary Table 1 contains primers only).
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit QUASARR-seq, SOLARR-seq and PRO-seq raw and processed data with resolvable ENCODE (or GEO/SRA) accessions, and add supplementary tables for the tested elements, the tested variants and the per-replicate RT-qPCR Cq values.

gaps.where: Every computational step - whole software environment
gaps.missing: No version number appears anywhere in the manuscript for any software. The only four software names in the entire text are fastp, biodatatools, edgeR and limma-voom, all unversioned; no interpreter (R or Python) version, no operating system, no conda environment file, no lockfile and no container image are mentioned. This is version_subtier 'floating' for every step and caps the whole paper below R-star.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock / pixi lock or a container digest pinning the interpreter and every package (fastp, biodatatools, edgeR, limma/voom and whatever computes the index formulas and statistics), and add a versions table to the Methods.

gaps.where: C1, C10, C12, C13 - reference resources
gaps.missing: No reference genome build (hg38/GRCh38 is never stated), no GENCODE release for the proximal/distal annotation cutoff, no accession for the K-562 DNase-seq DHS set used to define untranscribed elements, no version for the PWM collection taken from Adato & Sloutskin et al. (ElemeNT 2023), and no accession for the K-562 GRO-cap peak set (Core & Martins et al.) used to build the background base frequencies.
gaps.how_to_close: State the genome assembly and patch, the GENCODE release number, the ENCODE accession of the DNase-seq DHS set, the ElemeNT/PWM database version, and the accession or download URL (with date) of the GRO-cap peak set.

gaps.where: C5, C7, C13, C15 - undefined analysis parameters
gaps.missing: edgeR is invoked with no normalization method, design or filtering settings (C5). The uniform active element call pipeline never defines what 'significantly higher regulatory activity than the basal transcription level' means: no Z-score or p-value cutoff, no multiple-testing correction, no minimum barcode count (C7). No overlap tool or genome build is given for the reciprocal-overlap benchmarking (C13). No statistical software, version, one- vs two-sided convention or seed is given for any reported test (C15).
gaps.how_to_close: Record the exact command lines and the R session (sessionInfo) for the normalization and calling steps, state the active-call significance threshold and correction method explicitly, and name the statistics software with version.

gaps.missing: The barcode index-mapping and activity-measurement commands are externalized to an 'Extended Text' supplement ('with detailed commands and workflow found in the Extended Text') rather than to a versioned repository, so the operational detail sits outside the peer-reviewable main text and outside any executable artifact. The bioRxiv supporting-information listing exposed in the JATS XML shows only 'Supplementary Figures 1-9'.
gaps.how_to_close: Move the Extended Text command list into the code repository as an executable workflow (shell script, Snakemake or Nextflow) so the commands are runnable and version-controlled rather than prose.

gaps.where: SuRE and CRISPRa input data (C13, C16)
gaps.missing: Processed SuRE data are cited only to van Arensbergen et al. with no accession or download URL, and the processed CRISPRa RT-/ChIP-qPCR data were 'obtained from I. Hilton, Rice University' by personal communication - neither has a public identifier, so both inputs depend on author-to-author transfer.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the SuRE accession/DOI used, and deposit the reformatted CRISPRa quantification table as supplementary data with attribution to the original authors.

gaps.missing: Vector engineering, TRE cloning, eaBC-TRE-paBC library construction, K-562 culture and nucleofection, harvest-time optimization, library preparation and NovaSeq X Plus sequencing, SOLARR-seq assay construction and RT-qPCR bench work are physical steps, out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W, not verdicted.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness. Once the promised ENCODE deposition happens, the deposited QUASARR-seq/SOLARR-seq sequencing data becomes the reproducible computational entry point.
